convertibility_reason: Arbitrage/synthetic pair EA that exploits pricing discrepancies between a synthetic symbol and its constituent real symbols in real-time, requiring tick-level execution speed and broker-specific symbol availability that cannot be replicated in Python backtesting
custom_logic_notes: Arbitrage EA (ArbSint) that trades the price discrepancy between a synthetic broker symbol and its real constituent pairs. Opens opposing positions on synthetic vs real symbols when a pricing gap exceeds a threshold. Requires tick-level execution latency to capture arbitrage opportunities. Heavily dependent on broker offering the specific synthetic symbol and on execution speed - not backtestable with bar data. The file is binary-compiled (.ex5 format mislabeled as .mq5) so exact parameter values cannot be extracted.
python_conversion_notes: Not feasible for meaningful Python backtesting. Arbitrage EAs exploit real-time pricing discrepancies that disappear in historical data. The strategy depends on execution latency, broker-specific synthetic symbols, and simultaneous multi-symbol order routing. A Python conversion would require real-time tick data feeds, co-located execution, and multi-venue order management - effectively building a custom arbitrage platform rather than a backtestable strategy.
